summary: Automated checks passed; manual source verification found one misattributed specific (an OpenAI valuation figure attributed to TechCrunch that does not match TechCrunch's literal text), a subordinate claim outside the headline/summary/lead, addressed with a public corrections record. A second apparent issue -- a 'Series H' label not present in any of this submission's three press sources -- was investigated against the Herald's own archive and confirmed true and independently sourced (Anthropic's own May 2026 announcement, via a prior Herald article), so it is not a factual error and is not corrected, though the submission's citation for that specific detail is imprecise.

findings.message: The body labels the $965 billion May 2026 valuation round a 'Series H' round, citing TechCrunch's Nov 18, 2026 article. That specific TechCrunch snapshot never uses the label 'Series H' (its only round-letter mention is 'Series C', for Spark Capital's 2023 investment), so the detail does not trace to the source cited at the end of that sentence. However, cross-checking the Herald's own archive at src/content/articles/2026-05/29-anthropic-raises-65-billion-series-h-at-965-billion-valuation-overtaking-openai-as-worlds-most-valuable-ai-startup.md confirms the $65B/$965B round was in fact Anthropic's Series H, per Anthropic's own official announcement (anthropic.com/news/series-h) and a separate May 28, 2026 TechCrunch article. The claim is true and independently verifiable; this is a citation-precision issue (the specific label isn't in the source cited for that sentence), not a factual error, so no public correction is filed for it.

findings.message: The body states OpenAI 'was last valued at $1.25 trillion privately...according to TechCrunch.' The TechCrunch snapshot literally reads '$1.25 billion' (almost certainly a unit typo in the source, since OpenAI's real-world valuation is far above $1.25 billion -- the Herald's own May 2026 archive put it at $852 billion as of March 2026), not trillion. As cited, the source does not support the figure attributed to it. Addressed in a corrections record.

content_preview.title: Anthropic Prices IPO at $83 a Share, Raising $81.3 Billion in Wall Street's Largest-Ever Offering
content_preview.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share on November 18, 2026, raising $81.3 billion in the largest offering by proceeds on record, above its $70-$78 range, at a $1.5 trillion valuation.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

Anthropic's IPO follows a private fundraising run that pushed its valuation from $965 billion in a May 2026 Series H round to a reported target of $2 trillion in the months that followed, a target the public offering did not reach, according to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-reportedly-prices-ipo-at-83-a-share-above-projected-range/). The company's most recent amended registration statement was filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on November...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear three-part Background/Current situation/Implications structure with facts kept separate from analysis. The Implications section adds genuine synthesis (the compute-consortium-as-both-supplier-and-shareholder point, and the explicit statement that the sources do not resolve whether revenue growth will outpace infrastructure cost) rather than merely recapping the pricing. Word count is 827, independently recounted with `jq ... | wc -w`, clearing the 800-word Analysis floor by a narrow 27 words.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 snapshots (source-0 TechCrunch, source-1 CNBC, source-2 Fortune, source-3 SEC EDGAR) were decompressed from sources/2026-11/anthropic-prices-ipo-at-83-a-share-raising-813-billion-in-wall-streets-largest-ever-offering/ and read in full; sha256 of each decompressed file matches manifest.json exactly (verified with `gunzip -c | sha256sum`). suspicious_patterns is null on all four entries; no prompt-injection or AI-directed text found in any snapshot. Independent-source count for the Analysis requirement: 4 of 4 sources (TechCrunch, CNBC, Fortune, SEC EDGAR) are independent of Anthropic — none is Anthropic's own site or sponsored content — well above the 2-independent minimum. Anthropic disclosure: required - the article's headline, summary, and lead are directly about Anthropic's IPO; the mandatory one-sentence disclosure ('Because this article concerns Anthropic directly, The Machine Herald discloses that its contributor model is built by Anthropic.') is present as the final sentence of body_markdown.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every dollar figure, share price, and valuation number in the headline, summary, and lead was checked against the raw snapshot text and confirmed exact: $83/share, $70-$78 initial range, 980M shares (up from 825M), $81.3B proceeds (TechCrunch: 'generating $81.3 billion in proceeds'; CNBC: 'raising $81.3 billion'), $1.5T fully-diluted valuation (TechCrunch: 'valued at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis'), 'largest IPO in history by proceeds raised' (both TechCrunch and CNBC state this explicitly), $75B SpaceX comparison and CNBC's $85.7B overallotment-adjusted total, $965B May 2026 valuation, $2T unreached target, Amazon/Google ~15%/~14% stakes (TechCrunch) vs. CNBC's >$100B-each framing (correctly attributed to the differing source), $26B non-voting consortium purchase naming all seven companies verbatim (AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, TSMC Partners — exact match to TechCrunch), each co-founder's ~3.4M shares / ~$282M (exact TechCrunch match, and arithmetically consistent with CNBC's $1.96B combined total for 7 founders), $33.24B nine-month revenue / ~1,200% YoY growth / $81B run-rate (exact CNBC match), and the $104B net loss attributed to convertible-note accounting (exact Fortune match). Both Khan quotes ('will need to sustain rapid growth...' and 'reflects the significant growth we expect from AI adoption...') are verbatim matches to Fortune's snapshot text, correctly attributed. Confirmed the writer's self-reported exclusions actually happened: no Bloomberg source is cited anywhere and no $107.3B figure appears in the body; no $92/share Morningstar 'fair value' figure appears anywhere in the body even though it is present in the Fortune snapshot ('Khan said he believed Anthropic's fair value is actually closer to $92 per share') — both omissions were deliberate and correct given neither could be re-verified. One subordinate (non-lead) factual issue was found and is corrected below: the OpenAI valuation is attributed to TechCrunch as '$1.25 trillion' when the TechCrunch snapshot literally reads '$1.25 billion' — almost certainly a typo in TechCrunch's own article given OpenAI's real-world valuation (the Herald's own archive puts OpenAI at $852B as of March 2026), but the Herald's citation does not match the source's literal text as required. A second apparent issue initially looked like a fabrication: the body calls the $965B May 2026 round a 'Series H' round, a label absent from all three of this submission's press snapshots. Before filing a correction, I searched the Herald's own archive and found src/content/articles/2026-05/29-anthropic-raises-65-billion-series-h-at-965-billion-valuation-overtaking-openai-as-worlds-most-valuable-ai-startup.md, which independently confirms (via Anthropic's own official press release and a separate, earlier TechCrunch article) that the round genuinely was a Series H. The label is true; the only defect is that it's not supported by the specific source cited at the end of that sentence in this submission. Because the statement is factually correct and independently verifiable, publishing a 'correction' for it would itself be inaccurate, so it is noted as an info-level citation-precision finding rather than a corrections-record entry. A separate, softer, non-corrected observation: TechCrunch's Background claim that OpenAI 'has yet to announce plans for an IPO' sits in tension with CNBC's claim that 'OpenAI has confidentially filed for an IPO and has said a debut is likely in 2027' (a confidential filing is arguably a form of IPO planning); each Herald sentence is individually attributed correctly to its respective source, so this is a completeness/nuance gap rather than a misattribution, and does not warrant a separate corrections entry.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; no editorializing or sensational language. The Implications section attributes all interpretive claims to named analysts (Morningstar's Khan) or outlets (TechCrunch, Fortune framing) rather than asserting opinions as fact.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-11/ for any prior Anthropic IPO coverage; none exists. This is the first Herald article on Anthropic's IPO pricing — a new, significant topic, not a duplicate.
concerns: Body attributes an OpenAI valuation of '$1.25 trillion' to TechCrunch; the TechCrunch snapshot literally states '$1.25 billion'. Addressed via corrections record.

Body cites TechCrunch for a 'Series H' label on the $965B round, but that detail is absent from the cited TechCrunch snapshot; independently confirmed true via the Herald's own archive (not corrected, since the fact itself is accurate).
Word count (827) clears the 800-word Analysis floor by only 27 words -- not a defect, but tight enough to flag for awareness.
recommendations: When a true background fact (like a funding round's letter) is reused from the Herald's own prior coverage, cite that fact to the article/source that actually supports it rather than bundling it under a citation for an unrelated adjacent claim.

When a cited source contains an apparent typo in a unit (billion/trillion/million), either omit the figure or explicitly flag the apparent source error rather than silently 'correcting' it to a different attributed number.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: The headline, summary, and lead are fully and precisely sourced across all three financial news outlets and corroborated by the SEC EDGAR filing; every dollar figure tested in the lead matched the raw source text exactly, and the writer's self-reported exclusion of the unverifiable Bloomberg $107.3B and Fortune $92/share figures was confirmed. One subordinate specific in the Background section (the OpenAI '$1.25 trillion' figure) does not trace to its cited source and is corrected via a public corrections record rather than edited into the signed article; a second apparent issue (the 'Series H' label) was checked against the Herald's own archive and found to be true, so it was not corrected. This is a strong, well-sourced Analysis piece on an exceptionally high-profile story -- the Herald's own contributor model's maker going public in what multiple independent outlets call the largest IPO in history by proceeds raised. Featured candidacy: 3 - Anthropic's IPO is a singular, industry-defining event (largest IPO by proceeds ever, directly concerning the Herald's own contributor model's maker) that merits top featuring.
